questions.prompt: Why can't `canWrite` inside your Node code stop `bash -c 'rm -rf ~/old'` by itself?
options: Once bash runs as a separate program, your Node code cannot see the writes it makes
canWrite refuses every path under read-only
questions.explanation: The shell is a separate program. Only the kernel sees its writes, so the rules must be handed to the operating system through a runner before the command starts.

questions.prompt: The Seatbelt profile denies all file writes but then allows `/dev/null`. Why?
options: Shells constantly send unwanted output to /dev/null, and refusing it would break ordinary commands
It is where the profile is stored
Seatbelt requires at least one allowed path
It lets the model read secret files
questions.explanation: Commands like `cmd 2>/dev/null` write to /dev/null all the time. It is a harmless sink, so even read-only mode allows it.

questions.prompt: What does the `--` in `['bwrap', ...rules, '--', 'bash', '-c', cmd]` do?
options: It comments out the rest of the line
It tells bwrap to run in the background
It marks the end of the runner's own options, so everything after is the command to run
It separates read-only folders from writable ones
questions.explanation: The runner reads its own options up to `--`. Everything after is the original argument list, started inside the rules.
